qualityPolicy.tierOrder: 12 material questions, then 8 original STAR-aligned fallback questions

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which sentence is a command even though it does not use the word “please”?
choices: Did you close the gate?
Close the gate before the dog runs out.
The gate is beside the fence.
questions.answer: Close the gate before the dog runs out.
questions.explanation: A command tells someone to do something. This sentence gives a direction.
questions.sourceFact: Grammar: types of sentences (test Wednesday, Sept. 30)

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Mia wants to ask where her library book is. Which sentence does that job correctly?
choices: Where did I put my library book?
Put my library book on the desk.
My library book is on the desk.
questions.answer: Where did I put my library book?
questions.explanation: A question asks for information and ends with a question mark.
questions.sourceFact: Grammar: types of sentences (test Wednesday, Sept. 30)

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: The sentence “You finished the picture.” is a statement. Which revision turns it into a question?
choices: Did you finish the picture?
Finish the picture now.
You finished the picture!
questions.answer: Did you finish the picture?
questions.explanation: The revision asks for information instead of telling information.
questions.sourceFact: Grammar: types of sentences (test Wednesday, Sept. 30)

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: A teacher says, “Bring your reading log tomorrow.” Why is this a command?
choices: It gives a direction.
It asks for a reason.
It tells what already happened.
questions.answer: It gives a direction.
questions.explanation: Commands tell someone what to do.
questions.sourceFact: Grammar: types of sentences (test Wednesday, Sept. 30); Reading Log

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Little Flap peered through the leaves before moving closer. What does “peered” most likely mean?
choices: looked carefully
called loudly
flew quickly
questions.answer: looked carefully
questions.explanation: The context shows Little Flap looking through the leaves before deciding what to do.
questions.sourceFact: Vocabulary: action, afraid, depend, nervously, peered, perfectly, rescue, secret

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: A bird waited nervously before its first flight. Which detail best shows the meaning of “nervously”?
choices: Its wings shook a little.
It slept peacefully.
It sang the same song every morning.
questions.answer: Its wings shook a little.
questions.explanation: Shaking before a first flight is a clue that the bird feels worried or unsure.
questions.sourceFact: Vocabulary: action, afraid, depend, nervously, peered, perfectly, rescue, secret

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Baby birds depend on adults for food. Which sentence uses “depend” in the same way?
choices: Young plants need sunlight to grow.
A child paints a bright picture.
A bell rings at noon.
questions.answer: Young plants need sunlight to grow.
questions.explanation: To depend on something is to need or rely on it.
questions.sourceFact: Vocabulary: action, afraid, depend, nervously, peered, perfectly, rescue, secret

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which situation is the best example of a rescue?
choices: A firefighter carries a trapped kitten to safety.
A child hides a note under a pillow.
A runner practices before a race.
questions.answer: A firefighter carries a trapped kitten to safety.
questions.explanation: A rescue means helping someone or something get out of danger.
questions.sourceFact: Vocabulary: action, afraid, depend, nervously, peered, perfectly, rescue, secret

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: A small bird stood at the edge of a branch. It looked down, pulled its wings close, and took one slow step backward. Then an older bird moved beside it and waited. What can the reader infer about the small bird?
choices: It feels unsure about flying.
It is angry about the weather.
It is searching for food.
questions.answer: It feels unsure about flying.
questions.explanation: The bird steps backward and holds its wings close, which supports the inference that it feels unsure.
questions.sourceFact: Story: Little Flap Learns to Fly; Reading comprehension: visualize, theme

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Read: “The little bird stretched both wings, leaned into the wind, and lifted above the branch.” Which picture should a reader imagine?
choices: A bird rising into the air with its wings open.
A bird sleeping inside a nest.
A bird pecking seeds on the ground.
questions.answer: A bird rising into the air with its wings open.
questions.explanation: The action words “stretched,” “leaned,” and “lifted” describe the bird taking flight.
questions.sourceFact: Story: Little Flap Learns to Fly; Reading comprehension: visualize, theme

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: A young bird is afraid to try something new. It practices, gets encouragement, and finally succeeds. Which theme best fits?
choices: Courage can grow when you keep trying.
It is best to avoid every difficult task.
Winning is only possible without help.
questions.answer: Courage can grow when you keep trying.
questions.explanation: The character begins afraid but succeeds through practice and encouragement.
questions.sourceFact: Story: Little Flap Learns to Fly; Reading comprehension: visualize, theme

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Read: “Nora was afraid to climb the tall ladder. She took a breath, held the rail, and climbed one step at a time.” Which detail best shows Nora acts even though she is afraid?
choices: She climbs one step at a time.
The ladder is tall.
She takes a breath.
questions.answer: She climbs one step at a time.
questions.explanation: Climbing despite her fear is the strongest evidence that she acts with courage.
questions.sourceFact: Reading comprehension: visualize, theme; Vocabulary: afraid

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Beavers build dams across streams. The dams slow the water and create ponds. These ponds give beavers a safe place to build their homes. What is the main idea?
choices: Beaver dams change streams and help create safe homes.
Beavers eat only plants that grow beside ponds.
Streams always move too quickly for animals.
questions.answer: Beaver dams change streams and help create safe homes.
questions.explanation: The details explain what dams do and why they help beavers.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: comprehension strategies and constructing meaning

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Lena planted a bean seed. First she filled a cup with soil. Next she pushed the seed into the soil. Then she watered it. What did Lena do just before watering?
choices: She pushed the seed into the soil.
She filled a cup with water.
She picked a bean from the plant.
questions.answer: She pushed the seed into the soil.
questions.explanation: The passage says pushing the seed into the soil happened immediately before watering.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: comprehension strategies and constructing meaning

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: The trail was narrow, so the hikers walked in a single line. What does “narrow” mean here?
choices: not very wide
very noisy
easy to climb
questions.answer: not very wide
questions.explanation: Walking in a single line is a clue that the trail does not have much width.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: word knowledge and skills

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Kai looked at the dark clouds, zipped his jacket, and hurried to bring his bike into the garage. What is Kai most likely expecting?
choices: rain
a birthday party
a hot afternoon
questions.answer: rain
questions.explanation: Dark clouds and bringing the bike inside are clues that rain may be coming.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: comprehension strategies and constructing meaning

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: After Sam spilled the box of crayons, Priya knelt down and helped pick them up without being asked. What does this show about Priya?
choices: She is helpful.
She is impatient.
She is confused.
questions.answer: She is helpful.
questions.explanation: Helping without being asked shows a helpful character trait.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: analyzing literary text

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Why does the author write, “The leaves danced across the sidewalk”?
choices: To help the reader picture leaves blowing in the wind.
To explain that leaves can really dance like people.
To prove the sidewalk is moving.
questions.answer: To help the reader picture leaves blowing in the wind.
questions.explanation: The author uses person-like action to create a vivid picture of windblown leaves.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: understanding author’s craft

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Read: “Maya packed a flashlight, a map, and extra water before the hike.” Which detail best supports the idea that Maya prepared carefully?
choices: She packed several useful supplies.
She went on a hike.
She owns a flashlight.
questions.answer: She packed several useful supplies.
questions.explanation: Packing several useful items before leaving is direct evidence of careful preparation.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: comprehension strategies and constructing meaning

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: A turtle moves slowly on land but swims quickly in water. A rabbit runs quickly on land but does not swim well. How are the animals different?
choices: Each moves best in a different place.
Both move slowly everywhere.
Both swim better than they run.
questions.answer: Each moves best in a different place.
questions.explanation: The turtle is quicker in water, while the rabbit is quicker on land.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: comprehension strategies and constructing meaning

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which pair begins with the same two-letter consonant blend?
choices: flag — flip
frog — fog
clap — cap
questions.answer: flag — flip
questions.explanation: Both words begin with “fl.” The other pairs lose one sound from the blend.
questions.sourceFact: Phonics: 2-letter consonant blends

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which beginning blend makes a real word that fits the sentence? “The bird can ___y across the yard.”
choices: fl
br
cl
questions.answer: fl
questions.explanation: Adding “fl” makes “fly,” which fits the sentence.
questions.sourceFact: Story: Little Flap Learns to Fly; Phonics: 2-letter consonant blends

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: In which word can you hear both beginning consonant sounds without adding a vowel between them?
choices: stop
soap
top
questions.answer: stop
questions.explanation: In “stop,” the /s/ and /t/ sounds blend together at the beginning.
questions.sourceFact: Phonics: 2-letter consonant blends

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which choice contains two CVC words with the same middle vowel sound?
choices: map — cat
fly — flap
here — pet
questions.answer: map — cat
questions.explanation: Both “map” and “cat” have a consonant-vowel-consonant pattern and the short-a sound.
questions.sourceFact: Word structure: CVC words

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which word has the long-a sound?
choices: cake
cap
map
questions.answer: cake
questions.explanation: The final e changes the vowel sound in “cake” to long a.
questions.sourceFact: Friday, Oct. 2 test focus: short a / long a

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a word with the short-a sound?
choices: The cat sat by the bag.
Jake made a cake.
The rain came late.
questions.answer: The cat sat by the bag.
questions.explanation: “Cat,” “sat,” and “bag” all use the short-a sound.
questions.sourceFact: Friday, Oct. 2 test focus: short a / long a

questions.explanation: The starting amount must be 4 + 7 = 11, because 11 − 4 = 7.

questions.prompt: Which equation belongs to the same fact family as 5 + 7 = 12?
questions.explanation: The numbers 5, 7, and 12 make the related fact 12 − 7 = 5.

questions.prompt: Mia solves 12 − 8 by thinking, “8 + ___ = 12.” Which number completes her thinking?
questions.sourceFact: Math: Subtraction to 12 (test Tuesday, Sept. 29)

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: In the number 472, what value does the digit 7 have?
questions.explanation: The 7 is in the tens place, so its value is 70.

questions.explanation: All have 3 hundreds; 398 has the greatest tens digit.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Lena has 28 beads and gets 17 more. How many beads does she have now?
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Math public domain: Numbers and Operations

questions.prompt: What number comes next? 36, 41, 46, 51, ___
questions.explanation: The pattern adds 5 each time.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Soccer practice starts at 3:30 and lasts 45 minutes. What time does it end?
questions.explanation: Thirty minutes brings the time to 4:00, and 15 more minutes makes 4:15.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: A ribbon is 32 centimeters long. Mia cuts off 9 centimeters. How long is the ribbon now?
choices: 23 cm
41 cm
21 cm
questions.answer: 23 cm
questions.explanation: 32 − 9 = 23 centimeters.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Math public domain: Geometry and Measurement

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: A class survey shows 6 students chose apples, 9 chose bananas, and 4 chose grapes. How many more students chose bananas than grapes?
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Math public domain: Data Analysis, Statistics, and Probability

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: A lesson says Jesus gives us a new life called grace. Which statement best matches that idea?
choices: Grace helps us live as children of God.
Grace is a prize earned by winning.
Grace means never needing help.
questions.answer: Grace helps us live as children of God.
questions.explanation: The lesson connects grace with new life and living as children of God.
questions.sourceFact: Jesus gave us the new life of grace

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: The lesson compares Jesus to a seed that dies so a new plant can grow. What idea is the comparison teaching?
choices: Jesus died so we can have new life.
Seeds are the most important gift.
Plants never need water.
questions.answer: Jesus died so we can have new life.
questions.explanation: The seed comparison connects death followed by new life with Jesus giving us new life.
questions.sourceFact: Jesus is like a seed. A seed dies for a new plant to grow — Jesus died so we can have new life (grace)

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Which action best shows what it means to live as a disciple, a friend of Jesus?
choices: Include a lonely classmate even when no one tells you to.
Ignore someone who needs help.
Be kind only when a reward is offered.
questions.answer: Include a lonely classmate even when no one tells you to.
questions.explanation: Discipleship is shown through loving choices, not only by knowing the word.
questions.sourceFact: We are called to be disciples, friends of Jesus

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Why does the lesson say Mary is also our mother?
choices: She is Jesus’ mother and the mother of the Church.
She was one of the twelve apostles.
She wrote every story about Jesus.
questions.answer: She is Jesus’ mother and the mother of the Church.
questions.explanation: The source directly connects Mary’s motherhood of Jesus and the Church with her care for us.
questions.sourceFact: Mary is Jesus' mother and the mother of the Church so she is our mother too

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Which statement correctly explains the Trinity?
choices: One God in three Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
Three gods who sometimes work together
One Person with three different names
questions.answer: One God in three Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches one God in three Persons.
questions.sourceFact: Trinity: 3 persons in one God (Father, Son, Holy Spirit)

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: The lesson says people are made in God’s image and likeness. Which ability from the lesson best supports that idea?
choices: We can think, choose, and love.
We can run faster than every animal.
We never make mistakes.
questions.answer: We can think, choose, and love.
questions.explanation: The lesson names thinking, choosing, and loving as ways people reflect God’s image and likeness.
questions.sourceFact: We are made in God's image and likeness; we can think, choose, love

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: After a picnic, which choice best shows responsibility for God’s gift of creation?
choices: Pick up your trash and recycle what you can.
Leave trash because someone else may clean it.
Break branches so the park looks different.
questions.answer: Pick up your trash and recycle what you can.
questions.explanation: Caring for creation means taking responsible care of the world around us.
questions.sourceFact: It is our responsibility to take care of God's gifts of creation

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Which response best shows gratitude for a gift from God?
choices: Use it responsibly and thank God.
Waste it because more can be found.
Keep it only so nobody else can enjoy it.
questions.answer: Use it responsibly and thank God.
questions.explanation: The lesson connects God’s gifts with gratitude and responsible care.
questions.sourceFact: Gifts from God; We thank God for His gift of creation

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Which example shows using a sense to enjoy a gift of creation?
choices: Listening to birds sing in the morning.
Solving 8 + 4 on paper.
Remembering a phone number.
questions.answer: Listening to birds sing in the morning.
questions.explanation: Hearing birds uses the sense of hearing to enjoy creation.
questions.sourceFact: We use our senses to enjoy God's gifts

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Which idea best explains why the lesson calls Jesus our Savior?
choices: Jesus died for our sins and gives us new life.
Jesus taught people how to build houses.
Jesus won every contest he entered.
questions.answer: Jesus died for our sins and gives us new life.
questions.explanation: The lesson connects Jesus as Savior with dying for our sins and giving new life.
questions.sourceFact: Jesus died for our sins; He is our Savior

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: In the image of a vine and its branches, why must a branch stay connected to the vine?
choices: It receives what it needs to live and grow.
It becomes a different kind of plant.
It no longer needs water or sunlight.
questions.answer: It receives what it needs to live and grow.
questions.explanation: The vine-and-branches image teaches the importance of staying connected to the source of life.
questions.sourceFact: The parable of the vine and the branches

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Why does the lesson call Jesus God’s greatest gift to us?
choices: He shows us God’s love and teaches us how to live.
He makes every hard job disappear.
He gives people the most expensive things.
questions.answer: He shows us God’s love and teaches us how to live.
questions.explanation: The lesson says Jesus tells us about God, shows God’s love, and teaches us how to live.
questions.sourceFact: Jesus is God's greatest gift to us; he tells us about God and teaches us how to live

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: A paragraph explains how to wash your hands in five ordered steps. What is the author’s main purpose?
choices: to teach how to do something
to tell a funny story
to persuade readers to buy soap
questions.answer: to teach how to do something
questions.explanation: A list of ordered steps is written to explain a process.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: comprehension strategies and understanding author’s craft

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Read: “I tucked the note into my backpack and hurried to the bus.” Which clue shows the story is told by a character in the story?
choices: The narrator uses the word “I.”
The sentence mentions a backpack.
The action happens before a bus ride.
questions.answer: The narrator uses the word “I.”
questions.explanation: Using “I” shows a first-person narrator who is part of the story.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: analyzing literary text

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: The sidewalk was icy, so the school put salt on it. What was the cause?
choices: The sidewalk was icy.
The school used salt.
Students walked carefully.
questions.answer: The sidewalk was icy.
questions.explanation: The icy sidewalk caused the school to put down salt.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: comprehension strategies and constructing meaning

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Tess forgot her lunch. Her friend shared half a sandwich and some fruit. Tess thanked her and promised to return the favor. Which is the best summary?
choices: A friend helps Tess when she forgets her lunch.
Tess eats fruit every day at school.
A sandwich is cut into two equal pieces.
questions.answer: A friend helps Tess when she forgets her lunch.
questions.explanation: The best summary includes the main problem and the important response without extra details.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Reading public domain: comprehension strategies and constructing meaning

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: You have 2 quarters, 1 dime, and 3 pennies. How much money do you have?
questions.explanation: Two quarters are 50¢, plus 10¢ and 3¢ gives 63¢.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Math public domain: Geometry and Measurement

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which shape has exactly 4 sides and 4 right angles, but its sides do not all have to be the same length?
choices: rectangle
triangle
pentagon
questions.answer: rectangle
questions.explanation: A rectangle has four sides and four right angles; only a square requires all four sides to be equal.
questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Math public domain: Geometry and Measurement

questions.sourceFact: Renaissance Star Math public domain: Numbers and Operations
